body.statement: Computing \(D^{\star}\) is NP-hard even when \(\Gamma=0\), there is one future policy, all \(q_x\) are equal, and there are two actions, by a polynomial reduction from maximum coverage in which candidate policies encode subsets of \(\mathcal X\).
body.justification: The proposition imports the standard maximum-coverage complexity boundary and explains why exact search may require exponential certificates.
body.gap: HochbaumPathria1998 already studies maximum \(k\)-coverage and its greedy approximation. The proposition is a transparent reduction showing that the causal design contains that established problem at \(\Gamma=0\), not an independent hardness novelty claim.
body.consumer: Software users receive a principled boundary between exact certified search and scalable approximation.
